expression: sigma0*exp(-Delta/(k_B*(T + T_dis*(Delta/(Delta + k_B*T))**2/(((1 + beta_shape*(k_B*T/Delta))*(1 + gamma_cross*(k_B*T/Delta)/(1 + k_B*T/Delta)))*(1 + eta_barrier*Delta/(Delta + Delta_filter))))))
symbol_descriptions: DC electrical conductivity produced by thermally assisted hopping between localized electronic states
Characteristic hopping activation energy expressed in millielectronvolts
Temperature-independent conductivity prefactor for fixed carrier density, geometry, hopping attempt rate, and disorder statistics
Boltzmann constant expressed in millielectronvolts per kelvin
Disorder-renormalization temperature scale setting the strength of temperature-dependent apparent barrier softening
Dimensionless shape parameter that weakens disorder softening as the thermal-to-barrier ratio increases, representing competition between newly accessible and less-effective hopping-path subsets
Dimensionless crossover-broadening parameter quantifying an additional intermediate-theta loss of disorder-softening efficiency from less-effective newly accessed hopping paths
Dimensionless barrier-filtering strength that suppresses disorder-induced barrier softening for deep localized states
Barrier-energy crossover scale in millielectronvolts at which barrier-selective percolative filtering significantly reduces softening efficiency

new_symbol_range_suggestions.Delta_filter: positive, typically comparable to k_B*T_dis or the sampled Delta range

derivation_notes: The parent law is re-derived by relaxing the assumption that disorder softening has a universal crossover shape depending only on k_B*T/Delta. Barrier-selective percolative filtering is represented by making the softening coefficient effectively decrease with increasing absolute Delta through an extra suppression factor multiplying the existing softening-denominator structure.
change_summary: Added an explicit barrier-scale suppression of the disorder-softening contribution, so deep barriers remain closer to Arrhenius behavior over the same thermal fraction. This creates barrier-dependent curvature in sigma(T, Delta) without introducing new measured inputs.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: A single effective activation scale represents the disorder landscape, with disorder softening governed by one universal crossover profile that does not have an additional explicit dependence on the absolute barrier scale.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Barrier-selective percolative filtering can become less effective for deeper localized states because accessible alternative paths remain energetically too costly, so the disorder-induced reduction of apparent activation energy depends on absolute Delta as well as on k_B*T/Delta.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit eta_barrier -> 0, or approximately when Delta << Delta_filter so the added suppression factor tends to unity.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed Delta, conductivity is controlled by one smooth disorder-softened Arrhenius denominator whose temperature dependence follows a single shared crossover shape, so log(sigma) versus 1/T has one universal bending pattern after rescaling by k_B*T/Delta.
response_change.child_relation: Retain thermally assisted hopping and disorder softening, but relax the assumption that the softening strength is independent of barrier scale except through k_B*T/Delta; allow the efficiency of disorder-induced barrier reduction itself to weaken for sufficiently large Delta, producing barrier-dependent curvature in the apparent activation law.
response_change.observable_effect: Across low-Delta and high-Delta subsets, the temperature-induced softening of the apparent barrier bends log(sigma) differently: high-Delta samples retain closer-to-Arrhenius behavior deeper into the same k_B*T/Delta range, while low-Delta samples show earlier curvature/saturation. One shared parent parameter set cannot make the crossover curvature depend separately on Delta beyond the existing ratio structure.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when Delta spans a range comparable to and larger than k_B*T_dis and temperatures also reach intermediate theta = k_B*T/Delta ~ 0.1 to 1, where disorder softening is active but not fully saturated.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, different Delta slices can already show unequal curvature of log(sigma) versus 1/T at similar theta; in holdout, the same mechanism extends this contrast to larger Delta where the softening suppression becomes stronger.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added barrier-scale dependence vanishes, e.g. in the limit of zero strength for the new dependence or when Delta is small compared with its new crossover scale so the extra factor is effectively unity.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Barrier-dependent suppression of disorder softening in hopping transport
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Barrier-selective percolative filtering can become less effective for deeper localized states because accessible alternative paths remain energetically too costly, so the disorder-induced reduction of apparent activation energy depends on absolute Delta as well as on k_B*T/Delta.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient of the existing disorder-softening process now varies with Delta, changing the curvature of the scored mapping across Delta slices rather than merely rescaling conductivity or shifting one common crossover.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: A single universal temperature-crossover shape controls disorder softening for all barriers once expressed through k_B*T/Delta.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The disorder-softening coefficient itself weakens with increasing absolute barrier scale through a barrier-filtering factor.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: sigma0*exp(-Delta/(k_B*(T + T_dis*(Delta/(Delta + k_B*T))**2/((1 + beta_shape*(k_B*T/Delta))*(1 + gamma_cross*(k_B*T/Delta)/(1 + k_B*T/Delta))))))
evolution_contract.after_fragment: sigma0*exp(-Delta/(k_B*(T + T_dis*(Delta/(Delta + k_B*T))**2/(((1 + beta_shape*(k_B*T/Delta))*(1 + gamma_cross*(k_B*T/Delta)/(1 + k_B*T/Delta)))*(1 + eta_barrier*Delta/(Delta + Delta_filter))))))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when eta_barrier -> 0, or approximately for Delta << Delta_filter.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed theta = k_B*T/Delta in the active regime, increasing Delta now specifically suppresses the disorder-softening contribution, so log(sigma) versus 1/T becomes less curved for large-Delta samples than for small-Delta samples; this alters the target mapping sigma(T,Delta), not merely an auxiliary interpretation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's existing parameters cannot reproduce this contrast with a single shared parameter set because beta_shape and gamma_cross only reshape the common theta-dependent crossover, while T_dis sets one global softening scale. None of them introduces a separate monotone dependence of softening efficiency on absolute Delta at fixed theta, so unequal curvature across Delta slices is structurally unavailable in the parent.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when Delta spans a range comparable to and larger than k_B*T_dis and temperatures also reach intermediate theta = k_B*T/Delta ~ 0.1 to 1, where disorder softening is active but not fully saturated.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, different Delta slices can already show unequal curvature of log(sigma) versus 1/T at similar theta; in holdout, the same mechanism extends this contrast to larger Delta where the softening suppression becomes stronger.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added barrier-scale dependence vanishes, e.g. in the limit of zero strength for the new dependence or when Delta is small compared with its new crossover scale so the extra factor is effectively unity.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes a single universal temperature-crossover shape for disorder softening once expressed through k_B*T/Delta, with Delta affecting the response mainly through the Arrhenius numerator and the existing ratio factors; it omits the realistic possibility that very deep barriers are less efficiently softened by disorder-mediated pathway selection even at the same thermal fraction.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: A single effective activation scale represents the disorder landscape, with disorder softening governed by one universal crossover profile that does not have an additional explicit dependence on the absolute barrier scale.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Barrier-selective percolative filtering can become less effective for deeper localized states because accessible alternative paths remain energetically too costly, so the disorder-induced reduction of apparent activation energy depends on absolute Delta as well as on k_B*T/Delta.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed sigma0, k_B, T_dis, beta_shape, and gamma_cross, increasing T always increases sigma by lowering the effective Arrhenius denominator through one common softening law, while increasing Delta decreases sigma. The scientific gap is that the parent encodes only one phase of disorder-softening curvature across all barriers: once plotted against theta = k_B*T/Delta, every sample shares the same crossover shape apart from overall scaling by Delta. A realistic refinement is to relax that universal-shape assumption and let the disorder-softening efficiency itself depend on the absolute barrier scale. Varied conditions: T and Delta are independently sampled; carrier density, geometry, disorder statistics, and weak-field conditions remain fixed. Concrete contrast: for two samples measured over similar theta in the admissible range, one with Delta << k_B*T_dis and one with Delta >= k_B*T_dis, the child can show stronger bending away from simple Arrhenius behavior for the lower-Delta sample and delayed/smaller bending for the higher-Delta sample. The parent with one shared parameter set cannot reproduce such barrier-dependent curvature beyond its fixed rational dependence on theta. This changes the scored target mapping sigma(T,Delta), not merely an auxiliary interpretation. Limitation: this is most defensible when the experiment actually spans a broad enough Delta range; if all Delta are narrowly clustered, the added dependence may be hard to identify.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: Measure the dc conductivity of a disordered insulating solid while independently varying temperature and the characteristic energetic barrier associated with localized electronic states. The baseline response is governed by thermally assisted hopping of charge carriers between localized sites. Carrier density, sample geometry, and the statistical structure of the disorder are held fixed. The target is the instantaneous conductivity under each sampled condition.
